service.description:
ISO 12100 / ISO-TR 22100-4 mechanical-safety crosswalk: answers TR 22100-4 clause 3's guiding question ("can a cyber compromise through this connection reach a Safety function or cause a dangerous movement?") for a real Device, generically - joins the Device's real attack-vector connections (moqui.device.DeviceConnection with a physical-port driver - DcdUsbPhysical/DcdSerialPhysical/DcdSdCardPhysical - or a DcpMaintenance/DcpDiagnostics purpose, plus any org.moqui.cyber. CyberDeviceCommunicationFlow rows) against the linked Product's real ProductFeature/PftSafetyFunction rows (ISO 12100 6.2.11.4 safety functions, or the EPLAN SAFETYRELATED_* parameters from the plm-bom-import skill). No data is invented: a Device with no real vector or no real safety-function ProductFeature on record correctly returns that absence as a fact, not a fabricated "safe"/"exposed" verdict.
This is a MmtCodeDefinedFunction MathModel (MM_DEVICE_SAFETY_EXPOSURE, see CyberMachineGraphMetadataSeedData.xml), fifth reuse of the math-model-run-tracking pattern: a rule-based join, not a pure calculation, but its outcome is worth tracking the same way as check#ProductCategoryCompliance/check#DeviceGroupContinuityImpact.
